field_changes.before: Observed code site-assessment framework requires an applicant's sound assessment before specified local approvals for a new facility reasonably anticipated to require at least 100 MW of retail utility power. Sound impacts concern homes and schools within 500 feet of the facility property boundary; other resource assessments are optional, and utility substation/voltage information is also required subject to stated qualifications. The framework preserves the existing-approval/expansion exception; its phrase “does not exceed an additional 100 megawatts or more” is not converted into a definitive boundary here. The observed code publishes the framework as 15.2-2209.5 and cites chapters 567 and 568. SB94’s Chapter 568 print was not recovered in the initial cohort; the subsequently recovered approved print numbers the section 15.2-2209.4; the observed code numbers it 15.2-2209.5. The cause and legal effect of the numbering difference have not been independently determined. Later force is not independently confirmed.
field_changes.after: Observed code site-assessment framework requires an applicant's sound assessment before specified local approvals for a new facility reasonably anticipated to require at least 100 MW of retail utility power. Sound impacts concern homes and schools within 500 feet of the facility property boundary; other resource assessments are optional, and utility substation/voltage information is also required subject to stated qualifications. The framework preserves the existing-approval/expansion exception; its phrase “does not exceed an additional 100 megawatts or more” is not converted into a definitive boundary here. The observed code publishes the framework as 15.2-2209.5 and cites chapters 567 and 568. Direct comparison confirms that all seven subsections A-G of the retained Chapter 568 data-center text match the retained code text after whitespace normalization, although the chapter prints 15.2-2209.4 and the code publishes 15.2-2209.5. A separate enactment, Chapter 1075 (HB888, approved April22,2026), also adds 15.2-2209.4 for parking, which the observed code publishes at that number. This documents the same-number conflict and the observed allocation; formal editorial renumbering authority and later legal changes/current force have not been independently established.
